clue.text: National tax returns at end of spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: returns tells us the word for tax is read backwards

parts.note: to drain is to tax or exhaust

explanation.surface: Tax rebates are filed as the spring season closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns DRAIN into NIARD, which goes at the end of SPA. 'National' here means a citizen of a country, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, and a Spaniard is a citizen of Spain.

clue.text: Accent of Frenchman, one ignored by lover

indicators.note: ignored by means these pieces are left out of the lover word

parts.note: a mistress is a lover
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's accent goes unheeded by his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing M and I from MISTRESS leaves STRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is accent, the emphasis placed on a syllable.

clue.text: A lie about fellow being easy to talk to

indicators.note: about means the lie goes round the fellow letter

parts.note: a fable is an untruth, a lie

explanation.surface: A fib told about a chap who is friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means friendly and approachable, easy to talk to.

clue.text: Parliamentarian held in derision after being thrown in jail

indicators.note: held in puts the politician inside the scrambled word
thrown suggests the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP is ridiculed after being sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after being thrown' scrambles the word derision; 'held in' puts the Member of Parliament inside, and 'in jail' is the definition rather than a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprisoned means locked up, held in jail.

clue.text: Exercise supported by British PM almost becomes indecisive skirmish

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of what follows, so it is supported by it

parts.note: running is a form of exercise

indicators.note: almost means drop the last letter of the prime minister's name

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British prime minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: A fitness routine backed by a British leader turns into a messy fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A running battle is a fight that goes on without a decisive result.

clue.text: Mostly small change I left in drawer

indicators.note: mostly means take the word for small change without its final letter

parts.note: pence are small change in British money

explanation.surface: Someone leaves most of their loose coins in a desk drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims PENCE to PENC. 'drawer' is not a piece of furniture but one who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is something you draw with, so it is cryptically a drawer.

clue.text: Scoff when performances fail to start

indicators.note: fail to start means drop the first letter of the word

parts.note: feats are notable performances or achievements

explanation.surface: Someone jeers when a show doesn't begin.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to eat greedily, so scoff means eats.

clue.text: Guy opposed to chucking out new bread

parts.note: a chap is a guy, a man

indicators.note: chucking out means throwing the new letter out of the opposing word

parts.note: anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: A man is against throwing away fresh loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened bread from South Asia.

clue.text: Not at all recklessly

definitions.meaning: an emphatic refusal or denial, as in 'will I, hell'
with wild speed and abandon, as in driving furiously

explanation.definitionFit: Like hell is slang both for 'certainly not' and for doing something with furious, reckless energy.

clue.text: Shortly judge will give fine to soldiers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
F stands for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A judge will soon fine some soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon' but signals that the judge word is cut short: referee becomes ref.
explanation.definitionFit: Ref is the short form of referee, an umpire or judge in sport.

clue.text: God! Course taken by one lion creates terribly anxious spell

indicators.note: taken by places the course after the one-lion pair, as if they took it

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
one is the Roman numeral I
a lion is a big cat
a tack is a course in sailing

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a lion follows a route, causing great fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A panic attack is a sudden episode of overwhelming anxiety.

clue.text: Box for living here?

parts.note: a place where homeless people shelter in packing cases, so a box serves as a home

explanation.definitionFit: Cardboard city is a term for an area where homeless people sleep in cardboard boxes.

clue.text: Redevelopment of Bury is said to be of lesser importance

indicators.note: redevelopment suggests the letters of the words are rebuilt into a new shape

explanation.surface: A plan to rebuild the town of Bury is reportedly a minor matter.
explanation.walkthrough: BURY IS SAID is rearranged. Bury is a town in Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsidiary means secondary, of lesser importance than the main thing.

clue.text: Stand up in shower

definitions.meaning: an argument that won't hold up is said not to ..., so to ... is to stand up to scrutiny
a quick shower is a clean, a rinse of oneself

explanation.surface: Get up out of bed in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Wash means both to bear examination, as in 'that won't wash', and to clean oneself.

clue.text: Copper container with dirty top

indicators.note: top places the dirty word above the container in this down entry

parts.note: blue means risqué or dirty, as in blue jokes
a bottle is a container

explanation.surface: A grimy lid on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is not the metal but old slang for a policeman, also called a bluebottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is dated British slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform.

clue.text: Couple from Belfast really want to have a home

indicators.note: couple from takes a pair of letters, the first two, from the next word

parts.note: to long is to really want

explanation.surface: Two people from Northern Ireland's capital yearn for a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple from' gives BE, the first two letters of Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong somewhere is to have one's home or rightful place there.

clue.text: Grease is about taking part in dance in college

indicators.note: taking part in puts the reversed grease inside the dance word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: is about tells us the grease word turns round

parts.note: oil is grease or lubricant

explanation.surface: A slicked-back style turns up at a college dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' reverses the grease and 'taking part in' sets it inside the dance. Balliol is a college of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Balliol is one of the colleges that make up Oxford University.

clue.text: After accident tramp finds temporary place to sleep

indicators.note: after places the tramp word following the accident word

parts.note: a crash is an accident
to pad is to tramp, walk heavily

explanation.surface: A vagrant finds somewhere to stay after a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash pad is a place to sleep for a night or so.

clue.text: Current in water flowing at a coastal region

indicators.note: in places the current letter inside the flowing water

parts.note: a river is flowing water
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A tide moves through the sea along a shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: A riviera is a coastal strip, typically a fashionable resort coast.

clue.text: A sign that improves tigers' cages

indicators.note: cages says the answer is held within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A notice says the big cats' enclosures have been made better.
explanation.walkthrough: Read through the letters of 'improves tigers'' and the answer sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a trace or sign of something now gone.

clue.text: Meet to discuss this woman's dope-taking

indicators.note: taking means the woman takes the dope inside her

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
gen is British slang for information, also called dope

explanation.surface: A woman is suspected of taking drugs, and there will be a meeting about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts the dope inside the woman. 'dope' looks like drugs but means inside information, gen in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items a meeting is held to discuss.

clue.text: Mysterious man contracted to bring in fresh help

indicators.note: to bring in means the shortened man holds the scrambled letters inside
contracted means the man's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Dick is a man's name

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: An enigmatic man was hired to recruit new assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' shortens the man's name by its last letter; 'fresh' scrambles help, and 'to bring in' puts that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphic means obscure and ambiguous, like the oracle at Delphi.

clue.text: Raise hamsters perhaps

parts.note: hamsters are examples of pets, and the word pets written upwards, as in this down entry, gives step

explanation.surface: Breed some small rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, STEP put UP, and it spells PETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up is to increase or raise something.

clue.text: Ordinary person who's disliked and rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the word and is thrown out of the disliked person

parts.note: a so-and-so is a disliked or annoying person

explanation.surface: An unremarkable, unpopular person is turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AND from SO-AND-SO leaves SO SO; 'and' looks like a link but is the deleted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre, middling, merely ordinary.

clue.text: Limited room one may associate with a loft conversion?

definitions.text: Limited room one may associate with a loft conversion?

parts.words: Limited room one may associate with a loft conversion?
parts.note: a small single-room home with an artist's skylit workroom feel, the kind made by converting an attic

explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a small one-room apartment, often created by converting a loft space.

clue.text: Delay held up a celebration

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means the word is written upwards

parts.note: lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A party is postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special event.

clue.text: I must have posters for my study

definitions.text: I must have posters for my study

parts.words: I must have posters for my study
parts.note: posters are not wall pictures but things that are posted, items of mail whose stamps a collector studies

explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist is a stamp collector, who studies postage stamps.

clue.text: Remove bow from schooner with it

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a vessel, so remove its first letter

parts.note: a schooner is a kind of sailing ship

explanation.surface: Take the bow off a sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip is slang for fashionable, up to date, with it.

clue.text: Radio presenter reading out a couple of letters

indicators.note: reading out says the letters are spoken, so we write how they sound

parts.note: D and J are two letters of the alphabet, the usual abbreviation for disc jockey

explanation.surface: A broadcaster pronounces two letters on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A deejay is a disc jockey, who presents music on the radio.

clue.text: Prize for golfers or jockey, say, mounted on foremost of colts

indicators.note: say tells us the jockey word is spoken and spelt another way

parts.note: a jockey is a horse rider

indicators.note: foremost of takes the first letter of colts

parts.note: up means on horseback, mounted

explanation.surface: Golfers compete for a trophy, or a jockey rides out on the best of the young horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ryder Cup is a golf competition between Europe and the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ryder Cup is the trophy contested by European and American golf teams.
